This page sets out what is on file and how to plan your Queen's Arc renovation.

sections.heading: Planning your Queen's Arc interior
sections.text:
Queenstown is a mature, well-connected central-west town, and owners who buy or collect keys here often already know the neighbourhood. The first fit-out is still worth doing properly: a fitted kitchen that can take daily cooking, full-height bedroom wardrobes, an entry shoe cabinet, and a living-room storage wall, rather than a cluster of loose furniture. Maison specifies this as built-in carpentry, finished and photographed professionally, including closer material shots when you need to decide on a finish. We do not use IKEA-style furniture as the backbone of the home. No official floor plan is on file, so typologies are not listed, and we will not invent a typical Queen’s Arc layout or a heritage claim from the name.

We will not invent walking times to Queenstown town, to Holland, or to any MRT station. Nearby Maison pages in the wider west and central belt include Amberwood At Holland and CanningHill Piers; they are private-housing links, not typologies references for this HDB project. Check your block, facing and the HDB renovation rules before you plan blinds, a bench or any hacking.

After keys, inspect defects and apply for the HDB renovation permit before fabrication. A moderate carpentry scope is often planned at six to ten weeks on site after approvals, as an editorial planning figure only. WhatsApp Maison with your approved plan and any key letter you have. We are an independent designer and are not affiliated with HDB.
